reconcile.note: Gill restricts John 3:13's 'ascended' to bringing down heavenly knowledge, so the earlier removals of Enoch and Elijah pose no real exception.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg presses the wording directly: John denies anyone ascended to heaven before Jesus, yet Elijah was already taken up in the Kings narrative.

quotes.text: Had any man ever ascended to heaven before Jesus? Jesus: “No man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven” (John iii, 13). Then that story about Elijah is a fiction, is it?
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), "Had any man ever ascended to heaven before Jesus?", on John 3:13.

sides.snippet: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.
sides.verseText: Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.

sides.snippet: No one has ascended into heaven, but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man
sides.verseText: No one has ascended into heaven, but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
